entries.title: aggregate — groupBy + _count + avg
entries.sql: SELECT active, count() AS _count, math::mean(age) AS avgAge FROM user GROUP BY active;
entries.note: SurrealDB requires every groupBy key in the projection — the key is also the alias, so the compiler drops the redundant `AS active`.

entries.title: aggregate — groupBy an ALIAS (the key may be the output name)
entries.sql: SELECT cartName, count() AS _count, math::sum(_split_lines_quantity) AS total FROM (SELECT lines AS _split_lines, name AS cartName, lines[*].quantity AS _split_lines_quantity FROM cart SPLIT lines) GROUP BY cartName;
entries.note: SurrealDB accepts the alias OR the projected path as a group key; both spellings work.

entries.title: aggregate — groupAll over a split (UNWIND then GROUP)
entries.sql: SELECT count() AS _count, math::sum(_split_lines_quantity) AS total FROM (SELECT lines AS _split_lines, lines[*].quantity AS _split_lines_quantity FROM cart WHERE name = $p0 SPLIT lines) GROUP ALL;
entries.note: SPLIT and GROUP cannot share a SELECT: the split goes to an inner subquery. `where` filters the PARENT rows.

entries.note: The probe fetches limit+1 rows; `name` is the only selected column, so `id` rides along as the reserved `_keyset_0` alias — read for the cursor, stripped from `data`.

entries.title: upsert — generated id resolves the unique row, else creates (onMissing create)
entries.sql: UPSERT ((SELECT VALUE id FROM uuid_user WHERE email = $p0 LIMIT 1)[0] ?? type::record(s"uuid_user", rand::uuid())) MERGE $p1;

entries.title: update — set mode with an expression
update — select projects the returned row (server RETURN)
entries.sql: UPDATE user:aeon MERGE $p0 RETURN id, age;
entries.note: The projection rides the statement's own RETURN clause — fewer bytes than the whole row; the result type follows `select` like reads.

entries.title: update — select + return before (projected client-side)
entries.note: `RETURN BEFORE <proj>` is a parse error on the server, so the BEFORE row is decoded whole and the projection applied client-side.

entries.title: update — omit strips fields client-side
entries.note: `RETURN … OMIT` is a parse error in mutations: the row comes back whole and `omit` is applied after decoding.

entries.title: update — increment lowers to SET age += $p (one read-modify-write)
entries.note: `{ increment }`/`{ decrement }` adjust the existing value server-side — no lost update between a client read and write.

entries.title: update — append on an array field (SET tags += $p, one server write)
entries.note: `{ append }` is the compound assignment: it APPENDS without dedup, and the server keeps a UNIQUE index over the whole array correct. Use `{ union }` when you want dedup.

entries.title: update — remove from an array field (SET tags -= $p)
entries.note: `{ remove }` removes EVERY occurrence of the value in one server-side write.

entries.title: update — union on an array field (array::union — the DEDUPING merge)
entries.note: `+=` never dedups, so the deduping merge is `array::union(field, $p)`, computed by the server.

entries.title: update — assign one array index (SET tags[0] = $p)
upsert — a COMPOSITE unique index is a valid target (multi-tenant)
entries.sql: UPDATE account MERGE $p0 WHERE tenant = $p1 AND email = $p2;
entries.note: `email` is unique only within a tenant, so `[tenant, email]` IS the unique key — pass every field of the group; a partial `where` would match many rows and is refused.

entries.title: update — decrement + return before (SET age -= $p RETURN BEFORE)
entries.sql: UPDATE user:aeon SET age -= $p0 RETURN BEFORE;

entries.title: upsertDelta — create-or-update with the before/after envelope (onMissing create)
entries.sql: UPSERT user:aeon MERGE $p0 RETURN VALUE { before: $before, after: $after };
entries.note: ONE statement: `$before`/`$after` come from the same UPSERT, decoded into `record`/`before`/`delta`.

entries.title: upsertDelta — STRICT update never creates (the default)
entries.sql: UPDATE ONLY user:aeon MERGE $p0 RETURN VALUE { before: $before, after: $after };
entries.note: `onMissing: 'throw'` (the default) compiles `UPDATE ONLY`; a miss rejects `ResultNotFound`.

entries.title: upsertDelta — distinct create/update payloads (onMissing create)
entries.code:
(client) =>
        client.users.upsertDelta({
          where: { id: "user:aeon" },
          create: {
            id: "user:aeon",
            name: "A",
            email: "a@x",
            age: 30,
            active: true,
            tags: [],
            address: { city: "SP" },
          },
          update: { age: 31 },
          onMissing: "create",
        })
entries.note: Distinct branches branch first (LET/IF) and envelope EACH branch in one transactional round-trip.
